blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
High-stakes international deals have a quality that is difficult to name and impossible to rush. They are conversations more than transactions, conducted over months, sometimes years, between a small number of people who learn, in the process, to trust — or not trust — one another. The contract, at the end, is almost an afterthought; by the time it is signed, the real agreement has usually been reached long before.

What distinguishes the people who succeed at this level is not technical brilliance, although most of them have it. It is the ability to hold many things in mind at once: the commercial logic of the deal, the emotional state of the counterparty, the political pressures neither side fully controls, the small unspoken signals that something has shifted in the room. None of these can be outsourced.

The deepest discipline is patience — not because time always helps, but because the haste to close a large deal is almost always a sign that something has been missed. The best closers spend the final week looking not for what could make the deal bigger, but for what might quietly ruin it.

items.q: According to the text, how does the author characterise high-stakes deals?
items.why: "They are conversations more than transactions" — o vínculo e a confiança pesam mais que a mecânica da transação.

items.q: What does the text say sets the best dealmakers apart?
options: Their technical brilliance above all else
The ability to hold many things in mind at once
Their speed in reaching a signature
items.why: "It is the ability to hold many things in mind at once" — não é o brilhantismo técnico, ainda que a maioria o tenha.

items.q: By calling the contract "almost an afterthought", the author suggests that…
options: contracts are unnecessary in international deals
the substance of the agreement is settled well before it is signed
lawyers should be excluded from negotiations
the signature is the most important moment of the deal
items.why: Inferência: "the real agreement has usually been reached long before" — o documento apenas formaliza o que já foi acordado.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Moving quickly to close a large deal is usually a good sign.
Trust is built slowly between a small number of people.
Unspoken signals in the room matter to the outcome.
The final week deserves close, cautious attention.
items.why: Inferência: para o autor, "the haste to close a large deal is almost always a sign that something has been missed" — pressa é bandeira vermelha, não boa notícia.

items.q: What does the final paragraph imply about how the best closers use the last week?
options: They defend the deal against threats they may have overlooked
They pursue new terms to enlarge the deal
They hand the process over to their teams
items.why: Inferência: eles procuram "what might quietly ruin it" — protegem o acordo contra falhas ocultas em vez de ampliá-lo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James no fechamento do acordo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So we are in the final week, and I want to be very clear with the team about how I intend to spend it. Not chasing the last few points of value. Not reopening the pricing. I want us hunting for whatever might quietly kill this deal in the next six days.

Three years of conversations have brought us here, and the counterparty trusts us — or trusts us enough. That is fragile. One clumsy clause, one signal that we are suddenly in a hurry, and the whole thing cools overnight. People forget that at this stage confidence is the asset, not the contract.

So here is what I need. Read every schedule again, slowly. Talk to their operations lead, not just their legal team, because the resistance usually lives where the deal actually gets executed. And if any of you feel a vague unease that you cannot name yet — bring it to me. That instinct is worth more than another spreadsheet.

We do not rush the last mile. A deal this size is ruined far more often by haste than by patience.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does James say he intends to spend the final week?
options: Chasing the last few points of value
Reopening the pricing with the counterparty
Hunting for whatever might quietly kill the deal
Rewriting the whole contract from scratch
items.why: "I want us hunting for whatever might quietly kill this deal in the next six days."

items.q: According to James, what is the real asset at this stage?
items.why: "at this stage confidence is the asset, not the contract."

items.q: Why does James want the team to talk to the counterparty's operations lead, not only their legal team?
options: Because the legal team is unavailable
Because resistance usually lives where the deal actually gets executed
Because operations can lower the price
Because legal issues no longer matter
items.why: "the resistance usually lives where the deal actually gets executed."

items.q: What does James mean when he asks the team to bring him "a vague unease that you cannot name yet"?
options: He values an early instinct that something is wrong over more data
He wants the team to keep doubts to themselves
He is asking for a formal risk report
items.why: Inferência: "That instinct is worth more than another spreadsheet" — o pressentimento precoce, mesmo sem nome, vale mais que mais análise.

items.q: What is James's overall attitude toward the pace of closing?
options: He is eager to sign as quickly as possible
He is indifferent to how long it takes
He deliberately resists haste and protects patience
He wants to delay indefinitely to avoid risk
items.why: Inferência: "We do not rush the last mile… ruined far more often by haste than by patience" — ele defende cautela deliberada, não paralisia.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "This is a high-stakes negotiation, and a single misstep could cost us the account." High-stakes means…
options: involving serious risk and much to lose or gain
conducted at a very fast pace
items.why: High-stakes = de alto risco, em que muito está em jogo.

items.q: "By the time it was signed, the contract felt like an afterthought." An afterthought is…
options: something added late, almost as a formality
the most important part of the deal
items.why: Afterthought = acréscimo tardio, algo que vem depois, quase como formalidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We can automate the paperwork, but we cannot ___ the judgement that reads the room."
items.why: To outsource = terceirizar; o sentido é que esse discernimento não pode ser delegado a terceiros.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ to close before quarter-end nearly made us overlook a fatal clause."
items.why: Haste = pressa; a pressa quase os fez ignorar uma cláusula fatal.

items.q: "She caught an unspoken signal that the counterparty was losing confidence." Unspoken means…
items.why: Unspoken = não dito, comunicado sem palavras.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no fechamento de grandes acordos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the final terms before we announce." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Their operations lead pushed back on the delivery timeline." This means they…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the plan in the room, but nobody followed through on the side letter." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving another point off the price will not move the needle on their decision." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's not rush into signing before we have re-read every schedule." To rush into something means to…
options: do it too quickly, without enough care
hand it to the legal team
items.why: Rush into = precipitar-se, agir cedo demais sem a devida cautela — exatamente o que James quer evitar.
